text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Luton Town and Manchester United at Kenilworth Road.
Luton had started to pick up some form, drawing with both Burnley and Newcastle United either side of a 4-0 thrashing of Brighton.
However, the Hatters disappointed in their last league outing after suffering a 3-1 defeat at home to fellow relegation-threatened Sheffield United last weekend.
Rob Edwards’ side, who have played a game fewer, are a point clear of the relegation zone and 18th-placed Everton.

There was a sense of goodwill at the start of the new year around Man Utd, who progressed to the FA Cup fifth round and defeated West Ham and Wolves in the Premier League, along with a draw against top-four chasing Tottenham to mark an impressive opening to 2024.
That positivity has grown further after Erik ten Hag’s side secured a late 2-1 win over Aston Villa in their last outing.
The Red Devils sit sixth in the league table, although some six points away from fifth-placed Spurs.
Edwards makes two changes from the defeat against Sheffield United.
Mengi replaces Burke, while Chong comes in at right wing-back for Clark, with both of those players dropping to the bench.
However, there is another late enforced alteration as Adebayo, who suffered an injury in the warm-up, drops out for Woodrow.
Ten Hag names the same starting line-up, and bench, as the one that defeated Villa last time out.
Shaw starts despite limping off against Unai Emery’s men, while last weekend’s match-winner McTominay remains as a substitute.
Fernandes will be flanked by Garnacho and Rashford in behind Hojlund, who has scored in his last five Premier League games.
Luton have lost nine of their last 10 league games against United, with the exception being a 1-1 draw the last time they faced them at Kenilworth Road (April 1992).
Will it be more Hatters misery here? We shall see as kick-off is almost upon us...
Referee David Coote gets this Premier League clash under way!
GOOOOOOOOALLLLLLLL! UNITED STRIKE AFTER JUST A MINUTE! The Red Devils roar into an early 1-0 lead as Hojlund finds the net for a sixth straight Premier League game.
A long Casemiro clearance hangs in the sky before Bell makes a mess of his attempted hook away.
Hojlund bursts through the middle, rounding the stranded Kaminski before drilling a low left-footed effort into the open goal.
Chong dances down the left flank but hoists a left-footed delivery well over Onana's goal.
This has been a poor start from Luton.
Shaw's left-sided corner causes some carnage inside the hosts' area but Luton manage to clear as Casemiro lurks.
Ten Hag's side are well on top at Kenilworth Road.
SAVE! Almost a second for United.
The visitors play through the middle before Rashford unleashes a fizzing right-footed attempt.
Kaminski sees this one all the way, though, and beats away an unconvincing save with his right arm.

Hojlund, aged 21 years and 14 days has now scored for United in six consecutive Premier League matches and in the process has become the youngest player to ever achieve this feat, surpassing Joe Willock's record (21y 272d).
GOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! 2-0 UNITED! This could almost be game over for Luton, who have struggled to get going at Kenilworth Road.
Shaw angles a left-sided corner that is cleared at the near post.
Garnacho volleys from the edge of the area, although a wicked right-footed effort deflects off Hojlund’s chest and catches Kaminski going the wrong way.
The United striker appeared to mean it, too, and what a finish to double his account!
Garnacho takes the credit for the assist after his right-footed volley finds Hojlund, who finishes past Kaminski from a tight right-sided angle with an inventive goal off his chest.
United are unbeaten in their last 12 meetings with Luton in all competitions (W10 D2), since a 2-1 loss at Kenilworth Road in March 1987.
That streak appears set to continue here.
WIDE! United are in red-hot form.
Rashford glides over the halfway line, cutting past Barkley before ignoring two outside runners.
The United winger opts to drive a right-footed effort from the edge of the area but skews wide to Kaminski's left.
Lokonga curls over the top for Ogbene, who fails to control and Onana races out to collect the loose ball.
Garnacho is then felled in the middle by Bell, much to the annoyance of the home crowd.
This is the earliest United have been 2-0 up away from home in a Premier League game (six minutes and nine seconds).
What a start for Ten Hag's men!
GOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! LUTON PULL ONE BACK! What a chaotic start! The Hatters are back in this clash as they make it 2-1.
Chong drives from the inside left-hand channel before his right-footed strike deflects off Maguire.
The looping ball evades Shaw and Morris nips in front of Onana to head under the United goalkeeper.
The hosts have a lifeline.
Casemiro lifts over the top for Fernandes but overhits his pass out for a throw-in.
Kenilworth Road is rocking as Luton attempt to go blow-for-blow with United.
Woodrow is cautioned after attempting to delay the restart from United's free-kick just inside the visitors' half.
Morris has been directly involved in more Premier League goals than any other Luton player this season (seven goals, four assists), with four of his goals coming via the penalty spot.
He’s the first English player with four penalties in his debut Premier League campaign since Troy Deeney in 2015-16 (six).
Rashford loses his cool and wipes Ogbene out after an aerial challenge with Mengi.
The United winger is fortunate to escape a caution for that needless foul on the Luton attacker.
Shaw commits a cynical foul, barging into the way of Ogbene, who was powering down the right flank.
The United left-back joins Woodrow in the referee's book.
Barkley hovers over the wide free-kick before delivering towards the near post.
Osho makes the first contact but his flick-on travels harmlessly wide to Onana's right.
Morris has been involved in six goals in his last five Premier League matches (four goals two assists).
Can the Luton striker find another to drag the hosts back into this clash?
CHANCE! The ever-reliant Doughty whips in from the left-hand side, though Morris cannot hit the target when rising above Maguire with his header.
The Luton striker is the first player for the club to score in three consecutive Premier League matches, but can he go again for his side?
For all their early dominance, United are hardly in control now.
The hosts look a threat every time they get the ball down the flanks, with Varane and Maguire set for a testing end to this first half.
Doughty has already attempted a game-leading five crosses in this match.
The Luton wing-back has another go from out wide but, this time, Mengi cannot redirect towards Onana's goal.
Hojlund throws himself to the ground after a lunge by Bell, although penalty appeals fall on deaf ears.
The Luton supporters suggest United's striker is guilty of simulation, though referee Coote plays on without further action.
In all competitions, United have won five of their last six games, including their last four in a row.
The Red Devils last had a longer winning run between November 2022 and January 2023 (9 in a row).
HUGE CHANCE! Maguire gets away with one.
His short free-kick goes straight to Barkley, who releases Woodrow into the area on his left.
The Luton striker takes too long, though, and his left-footed drive is blocked behind for a corner without troubling Onana.
OVER! Doughty swings a left-sided corner towards the far post, where Osho is completely unmarked.
The Luton centre-back has escaped the attention of Mainoo, but can only head well over the United target with a disappointing effort.
Morris gestures with three fingers towards the referee, and not the maximum points available in basketball, after Casemiro makes it a trio of fouls.
The United midfielder continues without a card, though, much to the annoyance of the Luton striker.
There's no escaping this one.
Casemiro trips the marauding Bell and the referee has no option but to show a yellow card to the United midfielder.
Across their last seven Premier League matches, Luton averaged 15.1 shots per game, in comparison to the 10.3 shots they had on average in their first 16 matches.
The Hatters have also had 5.9 shots on target per game in those seven games, a big increase on the 2.6 per game they had in their first 16.
Can a change in mindset pay dividends here?
SO CLOSE! Garnacho tries a needless piece of skill and Morris intervenes in midfield.
The Luton striker drives towards the edge of the area before pulling a powerful left-footed effort narrowly wide to the right of goal.

After failing to score in the first half in 13 of their first 14 Premier League matches of the season, Luton have now scored in the first half in seven of their last 10 such matches, scoring a combined 10 goals across those 10 matches.
How is he not off? Casemiro lunges into a late sliding challenge on Barkley after a poor first touch.
The United midfielder is already on a caution but, somehow, referee Coote gives the Brazilian the benefit of the doubt on this occasion.
After somehow escaping a red, Casemiro is now seeing the same colour.
The United midfielder rips into Garnacho with a flurry of words exchanged between the pair as tensions seemingly rise in the visitors' camp.
This could be an interesting end to the half.
Only Tottenham (36 games) are on a longer scoring run in Premier League matches among current teams than Luton (12).
However, the Hatters have ended on the losing side in five of those matches (W4 D2) and a sixth could be on the way here.
What are you doing, Maguire? The United centre-back needlessly fells the onrushing Morris, earning a yellow card for a terribly timed tackle and also conceding a free-kick in a dangerous area.
Onana organises a four-man wall as United prepare for another free-kick onslaught.
Doughty and Barkley hover before the former whips a left-footed effort straight at the United defenders.
Rashford twists and turns before his prodded pass is blocked by Mengi.
Lokonga catches the United winger on his way passed him, with the England international staying down immediately after.
That has not impressed the Kenilworth Road crowd.
There will be four additional minutes to end this entertaining first half.
WIDE! Luton break with speed as Morris touches over the top for Doughty, who has acres of space before dragging a right-footed half-volley wide.
The hosts should be level here!
Another blow for United.
Shaw is unable to continue, as was the case last time out against Villa, and makes way for Lindelof.
The visiting defender will slot in as a makeshift left-back.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-2 MANCHESTER UNITED
Luton are well in this Premier League game at half-time, albeit trailing United 2-1 at Kenilworth Road.
Hojlund scored an early double and became the youngest player to find the net in six straight Premier League matches, though the hosts responded as Morris headed home after just 14 minutes.
Ten Hag's side know they have been in a contest.
Doughty, Osho and Morris have all gone close to levelling, with Edwards' side improving after the early double blow from United.
The Red Devils must respond in the second half.
Having watched a chaotic first period, Ten Hag makes a double switch at half-time.
Evans comes on for Maguire, who was already on a caution, at centre-back.
Casemiro was fortunate to not receive his marching orders before the break and the midfielder also comes off for McTominay.
United get the ball rolling again for the second half!
United have won their last 11 Premier League matches against newly promoted clubs, only conceding five goals in this run.
It’s their best winning run against promoted sides since a 12-match run between 2011 and 2013 under Sir Alex Ferguson.
Dalot angles a run in behind but fails to round the onrushing Kaminski, who recovers and intervenes.
Down the other end, Barkley drives straight at Onana from range.
United are unbeaten in their last 142 Premier League matches when leading at half-time (W122, D20) dating back to September 2014 against Leicester City (a 5-3 loss).
Will the Red Devils continue that imperious streak here?
Ogbene sneaks in behind the United defence but Chong heads over from the resulting right-wing cross.
It would not have counted either way, though, as the offside flag is up in the build-up.
Ten Hag must think United need another goal to win this game.
The Red Devils' defence does not look like withstanding this barrage of Luton attacks, with Doughty and Ogbene enjoying far too much time and space down the flanks.
Doughty whips an inviting left-sided delivery across the face of goal but Woodrow and Morris are unable to capitalise.
The Luton wing-back is repeatedly pacing past Dalot, whose defensive work still leaves much to be desired.
Chong's long-range strike deflects behind for a corner.
Doughty takes the right-sided set-piece towards the near post but Varane heads clear.
GOOD STOP! United break with speed after defending a Luton corner.
Hojlund bursts through the middle before offloading to Rashford, who chops inside and aims a left-footed drive towards the bottom-right corner.
Kaminski, however, is there to parry away a fine stretching save after seeing the ball late.
Ten Hag has won all nine of his Premier League games against newly promoted clubs, the best 100 per cent win ratio against those sides of any manager in Premier League history.
The only two managers to win their first 10 games against promoted clubs in the competition are Jose Mourinho (first 15) and Roberto Mancini (first 12).
WHAT A BLOCK! How have United not scored? Hojlund slots through for Fernandes, who catches Kaminski out and rounds the Luton goalkeeper.
An open goal awaits for the United playmaker but his right-footed drive is blocked by a last-ditch Lokonga tackle.
What a challenge!
Doughty has attempted 13 crosses in this match so far, 10 more than any other player on the pitch.
A cross from Fernandes at the other end, however, forces Osho to head behind for a corner.
SAVE! Fernandes takes some vocal opinions from the home crowd before delivering a corner towards the edge of the area.
Garnacho manages a touch out of his feet before driving a low right-footed attempt straight at Kaminski.
Fernandes has created 71 chances this season, more than any other player in the Premier League.
Garnacho twists and turns but fires a woeful left-footed effort well over from just outside the Luton box.
United have controlled the game in the last five minutes or so.
Doughty is unable to round Dalot and has to settle for a corner.
The Luton wing-back also takes the set-piece, crossing towards the far post from which United clear.
Ogbene tries his luck from the edge of the area but hits straight at Onana.
Clark has been brought on in place of former Manchester United player Chong with a little over 20 minutes to play.
Townsend is also brought on for Luton in place of Woodrow.
There is still plenty of time to find an equaliser - and indeed a winner.
Townsend, on the field for a matter of seconds, rather clumsily drags down Rashford on the edge of the Luton penalty area to earn himself a yellow card and concede a free-kick in shooting range.
The United free-kick comes to little but the visitors work a shooting chance for Garnacho.
His attempt from the edge of the box deflects wide for another corner.
The corner is just too high for Varane at the back post.
Townsend is then fouled as Luton are given a chance to reset.
Luton get the ball forward down the left, but Doughty is unable to pick out a team-mate with a deep cross into the area.
The hosts are struggling to gain any real momentum at the minute.
Mainoo is the latest player to be cautioned after lunging in on Clark, who was charging through on the United goal.
Replays show he actually got a touch to the ball first so that is very harsh.
CHANCE! The free-kick is just out of shooting range so Doughty crosses it into the box.
The initial ball is dealt with, but it comes back in from the right and lands at the feet of Osho, who is unable to make clean contact and Onana gathers down to his right.
SAVE!! Kaminski makes another superb stop to deny Hojlund his hat-trick.
Rashford slipped in Garnacho, who in turn played it to Hojlund, but the close-range effort is pretty much right at the Luton stopper.
Lindelof is cautioned for a pretty poor challenge in midfield.
The referee did well to let play continue before then reaching into his pocket.
Berry provides some fresh legs for Luton in place of Doughty.
United have been unable to find a way past Kaminski, meaning Luton still have a chance of snatching something from this game.
Time is fast running out for them to do so, though, as Lokonga fires one over the bar.
Luton win themselves a late corner as they start to increase the pressure on their opponents.
It is dealt with, however, as is the next delivery into the box.
United try to counter but it fizzles out.
Ogbene cuts in on his left and drives a shot over the crossbar.
Onana watched it all the way, but that is still a nervy moment for United.
There will be no hat-trick goal for Hojlund as he is taken off with four minutes of normal time remaining.
Amrabat is on to provide some midfield steel.
Osho is booked for dragging Rashford to the ground.
The United forward would have had a clean run through if not for that intervention.
Fernandes intercepts a pass out and strikes a low and hard drive just wide of Kaminski's target.
That would have sealed the points.
A corner drops to Ogbene but Amrabat is on him in a flash.
The referee has added on four minutes at the end of the contest.
Yet another corner is won, but this one is too deep and is again cleared.
Luton do not give up on it and Dalot has to turn the ball behind.
Here we go again...
Another corner, the same outcome as this latest delivery is also cleared.
United attack but Garnacho cannot turn the ball into the middle as it is cut out.
Fernandes basically passes his shot to Kaminski when he should have been running down the clock.
That allows Luton to get forward, and Ogbene's cross goes behind off a United player.
One last corner...
OFF THE BAR!!! Barkley gets his head to the corner and loops the ball onto the top of the crossbar.
So nearly a last-gasp equaliser for Luton!
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-2 MANCHESTER UNITED
Manchester United overcome Luton Town 2-1 at Kenilworth Road to make it four Premier League victories in a row and move back to within five points of the top four.
Hojlund scored twice for United in the opening seven minutes to put them on course for what looked like being a routine win.
However, Morris responded not long after and that is ultimately how the scoreline remained.
There was plenty of drama in between, though, as Kaminski made a number of saves and Barkley skimmed the crossbar at the other end of the field from pretty much the final act of the game.
Ten Hag's side now turn focus to the visit of Fulham next Saturday, while Luton - one point clear of Everton in the final relegation spot - travel to Liverpool on Wednesday.
That is all for today's live text coverage, thanks for joining.
